book.title: Deterministic Generation Handbook
book.author: Lin Xi

chapters.title: Chapter 1: Seeds
paragraphs: Everything begins with a number. Given the same seed, the universe unfolds along the same path — the first creed of deterministic generation.
The seed enters a pseudo-random sequence, spreading text line by line and filling colors block by block. No one truly 'creates' this content; it is merely 'found'.
Exercise at the end of this chapter: swap the seed for your birthday and see how the world differs.

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Texture
paragraphs: Texture is repetition plus perturbation. Pure repetition looks mechanical; pure randomness looks noisy; the middle ground is what we call 'natural'.
Perlin noise gives the classic answer to this middle path: fractal layering, each octave doubling the frequency and halving the amplitude.

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Names
paragraphs: Naming fictional people is the most delicate step: common enough to be believable, yet never colliding with a real neighbor.
All sample characters in this handbook come from combinations of six fictional surnames; they belong to no real person.

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Acceptance
paragraphs: Generation is only the beginning. The acceptance checklist verifies item by item: content legal, distribution even, edges do not crash, identical after restart.
The last item matters most — consistency is the only loyalty to a deterministic world.
